liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (3 reviews): The China into Rider here is the version released on Europe '72; Reviewer names this China into Rider the best ever [8][11][12]
- **Good Lovin'** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out a great Good Lovin' closing a long first set; Reviewer lists Good Lovin' among the top-notch versions of the night, alongside Tennessee Jed and He's Gone [11][15]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds this version a bit too loosely assembled, though they usually love the song; The night's big jam; the reviewer finds it by turns fierce and beautiful, going to incredible places [8][15]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Reviewer hears nearly flawless Sugaree, He's Gone and Bertha, with the band tightly in sync [12]
- **Sing Me Back Home** (1 review): Reviewer says the band gave Paris a taste of Nashville, one of the tour's best versions [12]
- **Me and Bobby McGee** (1 review): Sounds great here, with a gentle softness, even though it isn't the reviewer's usual favorite [8]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Called one of the best versions the reviewer has heard, with Weir in excellent voice [9]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Bobby and Pigpen trade lines at the end of the NFA/Goin' Down the Road/NFA; Pigpen's voice sounds weak [11]

## The recordings

- **gd72-05-03.sbd.masse.142.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 33 songs; 215 min; rated 4.81/5 by 36 [1]. Said about its sound: This Masse transfer has clean channels, unlike the other circulating version, which has left/right channel problems [16]
- **gd72-05-03.sbd.samaritano.21923.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 33 songs; 215 min; rated 4.07/5 by 14 [4]. Said about its sound: This Samaritano transfer has clean channels, unlike the other circulating version, which has left/right channel problems [17]
- **gd1972-05-03.sbd.samaritano.29082.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 29 songs; 193 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [5]. Said about its sound: Channels on the source drifted wildly, so patches were needed in places [5]
- **gd1972-05-03.sbd.masse.6453.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 33 songs; 215 min; rated 4.8/5 by 5 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer calls it their most-played Europe '72 show and a favorite Dead show overall [7]
- Reviewer pairs this show with May 4, 1972 as both showing the band at its peak [10]
- Reviewer considers this tour the band's best, with highlights every night [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-05-03.sbd.masse.142.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by J Norman and D Latvala; source: SBD > multitrack 2" MR > rough mix [1]. Also: Soundboard feed to 2-inch multitrack master reel, followed by a rough mix [1]
- **gd72-05-03.sbd.samaritano.21923.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Joe Samaritano; source: Soundboard>Master Reel (multi-track)->DAT x 5 [4]
- **gd1972-05-03.sbd.samaritano.29082.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Joe Samaritano; source: SBD > Master Reel (multi-track) [5]. Also: Transfer was de-clicked, de-popped and normalized in Cool Edit Pro 2.0; Patches for the damaged tracks can be taken from the Europe '72 CD [5]
- **gd1972-05-03.sbd.masse.6453.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Mike Masse; source: SBD > reel > DAT > CDR > EAC > shn [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1972-05-03 Olympia Theater, Paris, France](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/07/grateful-dead-1972-05-03-olympia.html) [19]
- Poster by The Record Centre: [Grateful Dead – Olympia Theatre, Paris, France 5/3/72 (6LP box set NEW SEALED US 2021 Record Store Day release 180 gm vi](https://therecordcentre.com/grateful-dead-olympia-theatre-paris-france-5-3-72-6lp-box-set-new-sealed-us-2021-record-store-day-release-180-gm-vinyl/) [20]
- Poster by www.popsike.com: [popsike.com - Login - vinyl records price guide](https://www.popsike.com/GRATEFUL-DEAD-LIVE-OLYMPIA-THEATRE-PARIS-FRANCE-5372-6-LPs-BOX-SET-RSD-2021/313565838239.html) [21]
- Poster by Discords.nl: [The Grateful Dead - Olympia Theatre, Paris, France (5/3/72) (LP Tweedehands)](https://discords.nl/products/the-grateful-dead-olympia-theatre-paris-france-5-3-72) [22]
